summary: Iteration 4 Razorpay subscription integration: 14/14 new tests PASSED, 53/53 full regression PASSED. Verified plans endpoint, create-order (success + role mismatch), HMAC-SHA256 signature verification (valid/invalid), idempotency, cross-user attack 403, paid-status NOT downgraded by later bad-signature attempts, legacy /subscription/activate returns 400 when Razorpay is enabled, and auth enforcement (401) on all subscription endpoints. Tests make real network calls to Razorpay TEST API (api.razorpay.com) — orders are created live, no charges incurred. MongoDB direct reset used to test idempotency safely.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py exceeds 1100 lines — should be split into modules (auth, clients, entries, bills, subscription) for maintainability.

razorpay_client is constructed at import time when RAZORPAY_ENABLED is True. If the Razorpay SDK ever performs network calls in __init__, this would block startup. Currently it does not, so this is informational only.

verify-payment computes HMAC and rejects bad signatures BEFORE checking that the order exists and belongs to the user. This is correct (constant-time signature check first), but means an attacker spamming bad signatures with arbitrary order_ids will create signature_failed audit rows only if a doc with that _id exists. Behavior is acceptable.

_activate_subscription always sets ends_at = now + 30 days. If a user pays before their trial expires, their remaining trial is forfeited. Consider max(now, current_ends_at) + 30 days for fairness. Minor product decision, not a bug.

seed_data_creation: Used existing seeded users from /app/memory/test_credentials.md (9999999991 iron_man, 9999999992 client). Tests create live Razorpay TEST orders (free, no charges). MongoDB user.subscription_status reset to 'trial' between activation tests to keep results deterministic.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Razorpay TEST keys live in /app/backend/.env (RAZORPAY_KEY_ID=rzp_test_T1rAXlvsSt3miO, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET=7krUcsTLvHw5m2rt2R8JtwAo). To simulate Razorpay's signed callback in Python: hmac.new(RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET.encode(), f'{order_id}|{payment_id}'.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest(). Each create-order call makes a real network call to api.razorpay.com — expect ~500ms latency. Use pymongo to reset user.subscription_status='trial' between activation tests so end-date assertions stay deterministic. The legacy /subscription/activate now intentionally returns 400 when RAZORPAY_ENABLED is True — test_flows.py was updated accordingly.
